author: THE BLADE EDITORIAL BOARD
title: Editorial: Enforce all gun laws - NewsBreak
text:
By THE BLADE EDITORIAL BOARD ,
41 minutes ago
There’s only so much local politicians can do about the permissive gun laws that make it easy in the United States to possess a weapon useful in carrying out mass shootings, like the gang shootout that occurred in the Old West End.
One thing that judges, prosecutors, and police can do is hold defendants accountable for what gun crimes do exist.
Both Ka Nye Taylor, 20, and Eljay Crisp-Carr, 20, were convicted in the last two years of gun-possession felonies and were given probation, also known as community control, instead of prison time. That should have been notice to Taylor and Crisp-Carr that they were headed directly into real prison time if they continued to have and use guns.
In retrospect, everyone would have been better off had they had gone to prison then.
We understand the importance of not having an overcrowded jail. And of correcting youth before they become adult offenders.
As reported by Blade politics and city hall writer Alice Momany, it’s not an easy call.
Lucas County Court of Common Pleas Judge Ian English, who heard Taylor’s previous case, said he handed down the only sentence available for that type of charge. When Taylor was found to have violated probation he was sent to the regional jail for 270 days, which cannot be faulted as a lenient sentence.
State Rep. Josh Williams (R., Sylvania Township), who is an attorney, said juveniles caught with firearms tend to get a slap on the wrist under juvenile sentencing guidelines.
He gave the example of a 15-year-old boy who committed a murder in Toledo with two prior gun-related offenses, for the second of which he received probation. Never having spent a day in detention, he’s in prison 15 years to life.
We don’t have the benefit of being able to review their juvenile records, if they have them, so we don’t know if their imperviousness to judicial mercy was evident from their background.
It would appear in hindsight that neither one of these young men grew in maturity or wisdom during their interaction with the court system.
Gun crimes have become a dangerous realm of wrongdoing. And guns in the hands of young thugs playing the part of gangsters is creating bedlam in our city, where homicides continue at the same rate as the last two years.
When someone is caught in possession of a gun that they know they are not legally permitted to have, the law should be enforced sternly out of awareness that death potentially awaits the next time this individual handles his or her illegal weapon.
Prosecutors in Toledo Municipal Court and Lucas County Common Pleas Court must make it clear to anyone who would commit a crime involving a gun that there will be little room for mitigation.
